## A. The four weeks

- **Week 1, Learn.** Slow walk-throughs, correct start stance, stable two-foot landings, deceleration. 70–85% effort on complex cuts.
- **Week 2, Build.** Quicker short bursts on drills already controlled. Introduce reaction cue games. Keep rep counts similar to week 1.
- **Week 3, Transfer.** Finish a shuffle with fielding or throwing. Controlled broad jump into a short acceleration as a substitute, once unlocked. Preserve rest.
- **Week 4, Integrate and assess.** Combine first step, cut and reaction with a catch or throw only while technique stays consistent. Retest the chosen measures under the same conditions as the baseline. Quality over volume.

## B. Safety rules that apply to every level

- Up to three quality high-intensity sessions a week, separated by recovery. Games and hard practices count toward that total, so a game or a hard practice replaces a dedicated session rather than adding to it.
- Short accelerations with generous rest. This is never sprint conditioning.
- Stop for pain, dizziness, loss of form or a clear drop in speed. Pain is not something to train through.
- A parent or coach supervises and checks the run-out and landing space is clear and level.
- A 20×15 ft indoor space is for short, controlled footwork, jumps, brakes and short reactions. Not full 10-yard sprints and not home-to-first tests.
- No heavy loading. Start with quiet two-foot landings; add single-leg work only with control.

Progression gates: Skater hop (landing); Broad jump into a short acceleration (landing + braking, outdoor only); Reactive partner cues (reaction + braking); Controlled single-leg hops (landing); next level (landing + braking + reaction). To advance, the last two completed sessions
must show a score of 2 on everything observed, with no high fatigue; pain at the most recent session blocks advancing with no override; a coach may
override a *non-pain* block with a written reason. One harder step a week.

## E. The two exercises with no library drill

Full draft write-ups are in DRILL-DRAFTS.md. They are **not** in the drill library and have **no video**.

| Draft | In one line | Safety stop | Approve |
|---|---|---|---|
| Skater Step and Stick | Step sideways, land on the outside foot, hold two quiet seconds; no hop until two sessions of controlled landings. 2 × 3 each side, 45–60 s rest. Cue: "step, soften, hold". | Knee collapses inward or any knee/ankle/hip pain. | ☐ as written ☐ edit ☐ no |
| Half-Circle Cut — Round the Cones | Three cones in a shallow arc, plant the outside foot and push at each. 2 each direction, 45–60 s rest. Cue: "plant, push, up". | Slipping, skidding, or knee/ankle pain; 70–85% effort in week one. | ☐ as written ☐ edit ☐ no |

## F. The indoor substitute (20 × 15 ft)

- 10-yard acceleration indoors: *Indoors: 3 reps of a controlled 2–3-yard takeoff and brake. Not a full sprint.* (the specification's own text).
- Falling start indoors (my proposal, replaces an unsafe 5-yard start in a 15 ft side): *Indoors: lean-and-catch. Lean forward from a standing stance, take two quick low steps (about 2 yards) and land balanced on two feet. Use the 20 ft length and keep 10 ft clear past the stop line. Grippy footwear, dry non-slip floor. If the floor is slick or the space is tight, skip it and add one wall-drive set instead.*
- Not allowed indoors: full 10-yard sprints, home-to-first tests, the broad-jump-into-sprint.
- The 2 yards and 10 ft clear are my numbers, not the source's. ☐ approve ☐ edit: ______ ☐ use the wall-drive fallback only
